title: skeletal-playbook-prototyper-and-gradual-remediator
author: Priya Shah
description:
Context: On-call teams repeatedly create minimal playbooks manually to triage noisy alerts. Small, well-scoped automations (scale up, circuit restart, cache flush) are useful but risky without staged approvals. This PR adds two cooperating pieces: (1) a Skeletal Playbook Prototyper that synthesizes a compact, human-friendly playbook skeleton from alert metadata and recent telemetry snippets; (2) a Gradual Remediator operator that can propose low-risk, staged remediation steps with safety gates (preflight checks, dry-run estimations, and timed incremental ramp) and rollback hints.

What it does (high level):
- Adds a CLI subcommand (incident-bot proto-playbook) and a UI quick-action to generate a minimal .playbook.yaml from alert context. The skeleton contains: intent summary, priority, minimum diagnostic commands, suggested next-action steps, and suggested observability assertions to validate each step.
- Implements a Gradual Remediator engine that models "safe ramps" for a small set of actions (replica_scale, pod_restart, cache_invalidate). Each action is expressed as a staged plan: pre-check → take small step → observe metrics → escalate/continue/rollback. Plans are advisory by default and require explicit approval to execute; a new flag --auto-lease allows limited auto-apply in low-risk environments.
- Adds heuristics to avoid fragility: action-risk scoring (based on service SLAs, historical variance), circuit-breaker to prevent repeated retries, and an emergency abort hook.
- Exposes telemetry hooks so the SLO dashboards can consume stage-level metrics for audit and postmortem.

Why: Reduce toil for on-call while keeping human-in-the-loop safeguards. Synthesis of a focused playbook speeds triage; staged remediations let responders do incremental, measurable actions with clear rollbacks.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default behavior is non-destructive (generate-only). Gradual Remediator requires a separate RBAC permission and an opt-in config value in the control plane. No runtime behavior changes happen unless an operator flips the enablement flag.

Related: ENG-5942 (prototyper feature), PM-881 (oncall flow improvements).

Files touched (summary): added new CLI handlers, new remediator core, small UI quick-action, docs and examples, and unit+integration tests.

Testing: unit test coverage for remediator planner and risk scorer; integration tests simulate a slow-surge alert and assert staged steps and abort behavior. Load tests show minimal CPU impact (~0.6% at 1000 simulated alerts/minute) when prototyper is enabled.

Release notes: New on-call tools: generate skeletal playbooks from alerts and an opt-in gradual remediator for safe, staged low-risk fixes.

Migration notes: Operators should review the new RBAC role: incident-bot.remediator.apply. To enable auto-apply in non-prod, set enable_gradual_remediator=true in the control plane config.
